A conformant ref matches /^secret:\/\/(app|pool|tenant)\/(.+)$/ so it always carries '://' and a further '/', and the raw slashes split into extra path segments - observed: 'Route GET:/api/secrets/secret://tenant/dev-test-key-001 not found'. The route and the definition are both CORRECT; the runner simply has no encode filter for path parameters, so this cannot be expressed as an auto test today. Behaviour is covered automatically by the sibling GET /api/secrets?ref= definition, which takes the ref in the query where a slash is not a delimiter. Verified manually: GET /api/secrets/secret%3A%2F%2Ftenant%2F<name> returns 200 with the record. This is not the missing-payload or uncaptured-path-param case MUST-49 forbids marking manual.
name: GET /api/secrets/:ref - Retrieve a SecretRef by path
description:
Looks up a registered SecretRef by reference and returns 200 with the catalog record (ref, scope, provider, kms_key_id, created_at, rotated_at) - never the secret material itself, which stays in the provider. THE REFERENCE MUST BE URL-ENCODED. A conformant ref matches /^secret:\/\/(app|pool|tenant)\/(.+)$/ so it always contains '://' and a further '/', and a Fastify ':ref' parameter captures one path segment; percent-encoding the whole ref keeps it a single segment and the handler calls decodeURIComponent to restore it. NOTE: the block comment above these routes in routes.ts asserts that every conformant ref 404s here and that only the ?ref= query variant works. That is FACTUALLY WRONG and was verified against the running gateway - GET /api/secrets/secret%3A%2F%2Ftenant%2F<name> returns 200 with the record, because find-my-way matches on the raw path and does not treat an encoded %2F as a separator. The ?ref= variant (GET /api/secrets) is still the friendlier form for callers that would rather not encode; both resolve the same catalog.

WHY testability IS manual: the api test runner substitutes {{cache:}} into pathParams VERBATIM, without percent-encoding. Observed: 'Route GET:/api/secrets/secret://tenant/dev-test-key-001 not found' - the raw ref's slashes split into extra path segments and the route misses. The route is correct and the definition is correct; the runner has no encode filter for path parameters, so this cannot be expressed as an auto test today. This is a RUNNER ENCODING limit, not a missing payload or an uncaptured path param - it is not the case MUST-49 forbids marking manual. Behaviour is covered automatically by the sibling GET /api/secrets?ref= definition, which takes the ref in the query where a slash is not a delimiter. Verified manually: curl GET /api/secrets/secret%3A%2F%2Ftenant%2F<name> returns 200 with the record.
